Read a layer as an rij matrix

Source: R/rij.R
read_rij_matrix.Rd

Reads one data layer as an rij matrix on a template raster (such as the national 1 km template), the form constechr uses to extract national data for an area of interest. An rij matrix is a sparse matrix of feature values: one row per feature (i), one column per template cell with data (j, a planning unit in prioritizr's terms), as made by prioritizr::rij_matrix(). A GeoTIFF on the template is converted; a prebuilt rij matrix saved as an .rds file (such as NAT_DATA's species layers) is read as it is.

Usage

read_rij_matrix(x, template, type = "auto")

Arguments

x

The layer: a path to a raster file (such as a GeoTIFF) or to an .rds file holding an rij matrix, or a SpatRaster. A raster must be on the template's grid (same CRS, extent and resolution); use align_raster() first if it is not. It may have several layers, one row each.

template

The template raster that defines the matrix's columns: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file. Only which of its cells have data (are not NA) is used, not its values.

type

What x holds, one of:

  • "auto" (the default): from x. A SpatRaster, or a file ending in .tif or .tiff, is a raster; a file ending in .rds is an rij matrix (case is ignored), as wtw-data-prep2 decided by file extension. Any other extension is an error; set type.

  • "raster": a raster in any format terra reads.

  • "rij": an .rds file holding an rij matrix, whatever its extension.

Value

A sparse matrix (Matrix::dgCMatrix) with one row per feature, named, and one column per template cell with data, without column names. Cells where a feature is 0 or NA are not stored.

Method

  • Columns: one per template cell with data (not NA), in terra's cell order (row by row from the top-left cell), so column j is the j-th template cell with data. Template cells that are NA have no column. This is the layout of prioritizr::rij_matrix() with the template as the planning units.

  • Raster layers: converted with prioritizr::rij_matrix(template, x) (in blocks of rows for large rasters). Each template cell with data takes the layer's value in the same cell: no resampling, reprojection or areas, so x must already be on the template's grid. NA in the layer becomes 0, zeros are not stored, and values are kept as they are (doubles, not rounded). Values in template cells that are NA are dropped.

  • Row names: for a path to a one-layer raster file, the file name without its extension (for example Forest_ha.tif gives Forest_ha), as wtw-data-prep2 named them, because layer names in national data are often generic (such as Band_1); for a file with several layers, or a SpatRaster, the layer names.

  • .rds files: read with base::readRDS() and returned unchanged. The file must hold a dgCMatrix with unique row names and one column per template cell with data; only the number of columns can be checked against the template, not that the matrix was built on it.

Method choices are recorded in ADR 0011. Converting rasters needs the prioritizr package, which is suggested, not imported.

See also

align_raster() to put a raster on the template's grid first.

Other rij: clip_rij_matrix(), extract_layers(), rij_matrix_to_raster()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
rij <- system.file("extdata", "rij.rds", package = "constechr")

# A prebuilt rij matrix: 3 features by the template's 96 cells with data
x <- read_rij_matrix(rij, template)
dim(x)
#> [1]  3 96
rownames(x)
#> [1] "sp_a"  "sp_b"  "cover"

# A GeoTIFF on the template, converted (needs prioritizr). The template
# itself gives one row, named after the file, holding each cell's number.
if (requireNamespace("prioritizr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  index <- read_rij_matrix(template, template)
  index[, 1:5]
}
#> [1] 3 4 5 6 7
